cells.tense: You are here with the pen while more than one thing is true at once.
cells.ask: Name one structure you can see was built on nothing — out loud or on paper, once — and let that be the whole act.
cells.core:
You can hold several true things at the same time and still know which one you're standing on. Nothing has to be argued down for that to work. What you say in the middle of this lands, partly because you're not forcing everything into one tidy answer first.

The false structure is coming apart around you, and you're not the one taking it apart. That part is worth noticing. Plenty of people meet a clearing like this by rebuilding something else fast, and you don't have to. What the moment asks is smaller: that the thing you can already see gets said. Put it in words while the ground is still open, rather than waiting until the openness closes over and the old shape starts looking reasonable again.
cells.sheetLine: You can see it clearly, and you can say so before the clarity fades.
cells.verb: Holding several true things at once without forcing them into one
cells.place: In the moment false structure comes down and the room is suddenly clear

cells.tense: You are bracing for a day when everything will finally be obvious and settled.
cells.ask: Pick one question you're still treating as open. Write the answer you'd bet on, date it, and don't explain it to anyone — including yourself.
cells.core:
You're holding more at once than anyone could carry, and some part of you is waiting for the day it all settles. So the deciding gets pushed forward — each conversation, each choice becomes a rehearsal for the moment you'll know. What you've perceived is already here, arriving in pieces that don't agree with each other.

That's the strain. When the many truths outrun the one you're steering by, you start living just ahead of your own life, checking what's coming instead of what's here. You don't lose the ability to see. You lose the ground you'd have to stand on to act on what you've seen. Choosing one thing to go on now is not the same as pretending the rest aren't true. It's the difference between holding everything and moving.
cells.sheetLine: You're waiting to be certain before you move. The waiting is the cost.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you and did not reopen.
cells.ask: Bring one true thing you've been keeping to yourself to another person — spoken, not written, however roughly it comes out.
cells.core:
Something cleared, and you didn't step through. You can feel the truth is still in you whenever the subject comes up, but it isn't moving out into anything or moving your life either. You can still tell true from false. That part is intact.

Somewhere the offering stopped, and the quiet that followed started to feel like the truth instead of a consequence. So the many truths stay private, and private truths stop being usable. They don't get tested, they don't get corrected, they don't get shared. Putting one of them in front of another person is not a performance and it doesn't have to be complete. It's the smallest way back to the world where what you know can do something.
cells.sheetLine: You know it and you've stopped saying it. That's the whole trouble.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in, and you're calling it someone else's hand.
cells.ask: Choose one call you've already made — quietly, without announcing it — and tell the person it touches that it was yours. One sentence is enough.
cells.core:
You've been reading this correctly for a while. You catch what's off in a room before anyone says it, you know which version of an account is true, and you've moved on most of it without stopping to claim that you were the one who moved. So it goes down as luck, or as the situation sorting itself out.

The deciding is running. Only the ownership of it isn't. That's a strange kind of tired — being the one who knows and rarely the one who decided. Naming one call as yours doesn't make you vain or loud. It just puts you back in contact with what you've already been doing, which is the difference between having judgment and being trusted with it.
cells.sheetLine: You've been deciding this. Say it was you.

attempts.check: The record gives no evidence of what the person has actually lived, so nothing in the core may name a past event, a person, or a feeling as fact — every line has to be recognisable-if-true, deniable-if-not. The reader could reasonably object that Discernment never feels like abundance at all, only noise, so the core leans on the mechanism (many truths held at once) and not on a mood. The asks survive a wrong read: each is one act available today with no money, no audience, no prior healing. The sentence that would serve me rather than them is any line about how rare or valuable their gift is — struck. I checked that Too Much and Too Little sit as opposite failures of the same holding: too much is bracing ahead toward a clearing that hasn't come, too little is standing at one that already passed.
